thread:
maria: Noting a regression in host-side p95 for tiny chat reqs after yesterday's kernel picker update. p95 jumped ~3x on short sequences (<50 tokens).

sam: Seen it too. Flame shows a lot more time in tokenization + repeated small grpc writes. syscalls dominate.

leo: I can repro locally when picker selects the new vectorized microkernel. It reduces throughput for tiny batches, probably increases branching in tokenizer prefetch.

jin: KV prefix cache misses also increased during the window. Fragmented request framing seems to drop our prefix heuristic and triggers full parse + extra KV lookups.

maria: Short-term plan: add a small write coalescer (writev) to reduce syscall churn, canary revert picker for 10% of traffic, and add a tiny-request mini-batch path that forces legacy kernel.

sam: I'll prototype writev coalesce today. Early local run: baseline p95 38ms -> post-picker 120ms -> with writev 58ms. Helps a lot but not all.

leo: I'll add picker toggle + mini-batcher PR (detect seq<64 tokens, wait up to 2ms to form micro-batch).

jin: I'll surface KV prefix hit metric and add an alert for tiny-workload p95 > 80ms. Also will add a nightly tiny-request perf job.

deploy-bot: canary deploy: 10% traffic -> kernel_picker=legacy for service host-proxy @ 2026-03-23T17:00Z.

maria: Reconvene in 90m with canary numbers. If tail improves we roll. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
